cohort: The study included 241 term newborns, consisting of 121 infants born to mothers with reported drug consumption and 120 matched newborns of mothers without drug addiction, all born at the Maternity Hospital of Nancy between 2002 and 2018.
finding: Newborns exposed to maternal drug consumption during pregnancy showed significantly increased 17-OHP levels at neonatal screening and were smaller, lighter, had smaller head circumferences, and lower Apgar scores compared to unexposed newborns, with no influence of withdrawal syndrome on 17-OHP levels.
birth_weight: Measured as a comparative outcome, drug-exposed newborns were significantly lighter (p=0.0001).
